title: Write-through: the write isn't done until cache and database both have it
caption: Reads of written keys are always fresh, but every write pays two round trips.

messages.label: SET price:7 = 19.99
messages.note: The write goes to the cache first (or a cache library writes both).

messages.label: UPDATE price = 19.99
messages.note: Then synchronously to the database, the source of truth.

messages.label: ack to the caller
messages.note: Only after both succeed. Write latency is roughly cache + database.

messages.label: GET price:7 (later read)
messages.note: A read right after the write is a hit with the new value: no stale window for keys you wrote.

scenarios.name: Alternative: update DB, then DEL
scenarios.summary: Cache-aside writes skip the cache: commit to the database and delete the key. Writes are cheaper, but the next read pays a miss.
scenarios.caption: Write-through keeps written keys warm; delete-on-write keeps the cache simple and only caches what is read.

messages.label: UPDATE price = 19.99
messages.note: The database is written first: it is the source of truth.

messages.label: DEL price:7
messages.note: Drop the old copy instead of writing the new one.

messages.label: GET price:7 (later read)
messages.note: The next read misses once and reloads 19.99 from the database.

scenarios.name: Database write fails
scenarios.summary: If the cache is written first and the database then fails, the cache serves a value that was never committed.

messages.label: SET price:7 = 19.99
messages.note: The cache accepts the new price.

messages.label: UPDATE price = 19.99
messages.note: The database rejects the write (constraint, timeout, failover).

messages.label: GET price:7 (other user)
messages.note: Readers now see 19.99, a price the database doesn't have.

messages.label: fix: DB first, then cache
messages.note: Write the database first, and on any error delete the key rather than leaving a guess in it.

scenarios.name: Risk: caching every write
scenarios.summary: Write-through caches every key you write, even ones nobody reads, and those can evict the hot keys that earn the cache its keep.

messages.label: SET log:… (×10 000/s)
messages.note: A write-heavy table goes through the cache too.

messages.label: evicts hot keys (LRU)
messages.note: Memory fills with written-once keys; popular keys get evicted and the hit rate drops.

messages.label: more misses reach the DB
messages.note: Write latency also went up, for no read benefit.

messages.label: TTL on written keys
messages.note: Mitigation: write-through only for read-heavy keys, a short TTL for the rest, or write-around (DB only).
